lessons_applied: HEADLINE PROCESS VALIDATED, NOT CASHED: the flagged 2.273 snapshot beat the 2.05-2.10 close (+10.9% raw / +4.5% no-vig) and Portland won - but the prediction-market ask moved above the 45c stand-down before the user could bet, so the slip's fill rule said no bet and the user correctly passed. Prediction-market discounts decay fast: they are real edge AND a narrow execution window. Keep them shop-only; treat every pm price as minutes-fresh or dead.

STALE-QUOTE PROVENANCE (graded miss): the 'CHC 1.62' Saturday quote was contradicted by every closing book (NYY -125/-132). Likely a leftover Friday line - same-series prior-day trap, but in a BOOK quote, not a news line. Rule extension: every anchor quote entering a slate must carry book + explicit date-stamp; un-stamped quotes get the conflict treatment. The refusal held for the right reason.

OFF-MARKET TOTAL (graded miss): our CWS@TB 8.5 total closed 7.5-8 - a full run off. Totals move with pitching/weather all day; a single morning number can't anchor an evening total. Same-day re-verification or no total pricing.

Fill discipline works end-to-end: post-hoc pm verification is impossible (403 walls), so the slip's printed stand-down line is the binding contract and the user's execution report is the fill oracle. It did its job - ask moved, user stood down, a would-have-won bet stays unbooked because the price wasn't there. Grade orders on fills, never on hindsight.

Model-side humility: three graded upsets vs our lines (Sky 28.7%, Musayev 29.0%, Medic 77.6% loser) but 11-market Brier still tracks the close. No parameter change - Walters rule, sample far below Buchdahl's floor.

lessons_applied: ADVERSE SELECTION ON LIMIT ORDERS (graded, n=1 - no parameter change yet): the only order that filled (Liberty 1.278) cashed with NEGATIVE no-vig CLV, because a drifting line fills your order exactly when the market moves through it. The two orders the market never came to would both have lost. Direction of drift is information; consider requiring re-verification (not just a resting trigger) before any favorite order is deemed filled.

Day-old derived boards decay: our WNBA fair (off Sunday night's derived -450) missed the Monday close by 6pts - the card's worst line. Single-book implied-prob boards get a freshness haircut going forward: note-only until a second graded instance (Walters rule).

Registered totals went 0-for-2 directionally (15 runs vs under-8.5 lean; 6 runs vs over-8 lean) - totals remain the model's weakest market; keep them order-only unless a two-sided fresh quote and a model total both exist.
The garbled-board flag process (reject incoherent quotes pre-slate, grade the rejection at the close) worked first try - SD@ARI. Keep flagging rather than silently dropping.
Deadline effects were real but did not invalidate any priced premise (no probable starter changed); the slate-wide caveat was the right treatment.
